    "description": "## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-842` → `main`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:11:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #842
## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

## PR Description

Closes #842
## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.

- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.

    "description": "## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## PR Description

## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.

## PR Description

Closes #842
## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

    "description": "## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-842` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7

- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:11:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #842
## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #842
## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## PR Description

## gh-842 — Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever

### Root Cause
- A dispatched CI run cancelled while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) leaves its `in_progress` check-runs on the PR head forever. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts hold `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` even though the head carries green terminal entries from an earlier run (live fa #1457: ~2h BLOCKED, resolved only by an operator nudge).
- `validate_pr`'s green-cover guards accepted a completed-green dispatched run as proof "the blocker is not this CI": `skipIfGreenCi` skipped re-dispatch and `skipIfValidatedHead` armed without dispatching. Both deadlock under ghosts — the green run's entries are shadowed on the gate, so no rule ever re-dispatches. gh-821's zombie sweep missed it because its run-level probe reads green (the newest *existing* run is the old green one).

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (new, pure): classifies a head's check-runs — a pending check-run is a ZOMBIE when its backing run (id from `details_url`) is absent from the head's run list (deleted/404), concluded `cancelled`, concluded non-cancelled past a 5-min propagation grace, or link-less and stale >30 min (bridge stamp whose run died). Active runs, fresh stamps, lag windows and probe errors are LIVE — AC2: a genuinely in-progress run is never disturbed.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `headCheckRunZombies()` probe (bridge check-runs tool + existing head-run rollup; degraded probe keeps legacy behavior, retry next tick). In `validate_pr`, BOTH the `skipIfGreenCi` green-cover skip and the `skipIfValidatedHead` latch-skip are VOIDED when zombies hold the gate — the contexts count as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and the action falls through to the normal guarded dispatch; the fresh stamps become the latest per context and override the ghosts.
- `sm_github.json`: gh-842 VOID paragraphs appended to the `validate-armed` / `revalidate-armed-green` rule descriptions (livedoc convention).

### Test Coverage
- L1 (`test_checkRunZombies.js`, 19 tests): run-404 / cancelled / stale-no-runner / run-concluded zombies; AC2 live cases (active run, fresh stamp, propagation lag, probe error, unparseable timestamp); knobs; the real #1457 timeline replay (3 ghost contexts + green terminal entries ⇒ 3 zombies).
- L2 (`test_smAgent.js`): #1457 replay through `validate_pr` — ghost-held head ⇒ re-dispatch fires (AC1, both the armed green-cover and the unarmed latch-skip shapes); AC2 — a live kicker run behind the pending check keeps the skip (no double-dispatch, AC3).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — **2468 passed, 0 failed** (re-verified after the final tree state; pack require-gate probes green).

### Notes
- AC3 holds structurally: the voided skips fall through to the unchanged dispatch path — active-run probe, gh-748 race guard, action-time mutex re-check and limit-1 rule pacing all still apply.
- The optional belt (posting `cancelled` conclusions on cancel paths) was deliberately not implemented — detection + re-dispatch cures the gate within one tick; keeping the fix minimal.
- Knobs: `jobParams.checkRunZombieStaleMinutes` (default 30), `jobParams.checkRunZombieGraceMinutes` (default 5).
- AC4 (live soak) is observed-after-ship per the ticket's own test plan.

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
