# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

Good conventions documented. Check the smProvider usage of github_get_commit_check_runs to verify `mcpParse(res).check_runs` shape — the new headCheckRunsSafe uses `mcpParse(res)` then `.check_runs`. Let me check smProvider line 271.
{"command":"sed -n 260,285p js/common/smProvider.js; echo ---; grep -n \"commitCheckRuns\" js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js | head -3"}

Good — the tool shape is consistent. Now let me check a few remaining review concerns:

1. **Double probe per tick per skipping candidate**: `headCheckRunZombies` makes 2 extra gh api calls (check-runs + full head run list). The green-cover guard is on revalidate-armed-green (checks=green, not CLEAN); latch-skip is on validate-armed. For each candidate that reaches these guards with vProbe.green, 2 more calls. Also note: `headCheckRunZombies` re-fetches `headWorkflowRunsSafe` even though `probeDispatchedState` already fetched the dispatched-run list (workflow-filtered). The full-head list includes all events, so a refetch is needed, but only filtered per_page=50 runs. Cost is modest (2 calls per candidate per tick, only when green). Acceptable — could note as SUGGESTION but honestly within established probe family patterns. Skip.

2. **Ordering issue — the voided green-cover fall-through**: after void, code falls through to... what comes next? The latch-skip guard (if rule has skipIfValidatedHead), then red-defer, gh-748 race guard, cancelStaleDispatchedRuns, dispatch. Wait — the green-cover guard `continue`s normally; when voided it falls to the latch-skip check. Minor edge, only in tests.

4. **`_startedAtMs` in stale branch: `now - started` — if started is in the future (clock skew), `now - started` negative, not > staleMs → live. OK fail-safe.

5. **In the `run-concluded` branch, `endTs` uses `state.updated_at || state.updated_at || state.created_at`** — the duplicated `updated_at` is clearly a typo for `updatedAt`. Since gh api returns snake_case, no runtime impact today. SUGGESTION.

6. **`isPendingCheckRun` treats check-run with status 'completed' and no conclusion as pending?** PENDING_STATUSES doesn't include 'completed', so no. Good.

7. **What about `waiting` status on check runs**: included. Fine.

8. **Grace logic**: for a run concluded non-cancelled with unparseable updated_at, `lag === null` → zombie ('run-concluded'). Hmm: `if (lag !== null && lag >= 0 && lag <= graceMs) live; else zombie`. So unparseable timestamp → zombie. Is that fail-safe? A run that completed successfully but has an unparseable updated_at would be classified zombie → re-dispatch. The comment says "Unparseable/young → fail safe" but that's for the link-less branch. For run-concluded with unparseable ts, it classifies as zombie — arguably acceptable (the run did end and the check never got concluded — that IS the ghost signature). Actually wait — if the run concluded successfully and the check-run is still pending, that means the conclusion propagation either hasn't happened or failed. Given `updated_at` unparseable, can't measure grace. Classifying as zombie after the run completed is defensible. But could also be a propagation lag > unknown. Minor; not worth flagging beyond maybe a note. Actually, gh api `updated_at` is always ISO — fine.

9. **Potential double-dispatch concern (AC3)**: The voided path re-dispatches, and stampValidationChecksForModule stamps fresh in_progress checks. The next tick, the fresh stamp is young → live, green-cover skip... wait, next tick vProbe.green: the dispatched run is active → vProbe.active → skip. OK.

10. **`headCheckRunZombies` returns early `{zombies: [], ...}` when `!checkRuns.length`** — skips the run-list fetch. Fine.

11. **probeDispatchedState `vProbe.green`** — the void only fires when vProbe.green. If the rollup is green but the dispatched probe isn't (e.g., run-level zombie per gh-821), other rules handle it. Scope OK.

12. **The latch-skip void**: when voided, falls through to dispatch — but note the latch-skip arm applied `ai_validating` label; the dispatch path also adds `ai_validating` post-dispatch. Good.

13. **sm_github.json livedoc updates** — appended paragraphs to validate-armed and revalidate-armed-green descriptions. Matches convention.

14. One more check — `headCheckRunsSafe` warns with `console.warn` — is console.warn available in GraalJS here? Other code uses console.warn (e.g., line 4695). Fine.

15. `github_get_commit_check_runs` in test mock: test_smAgent's github mock at line 265 handles it. Good.

16. Line numbers for inline comments: The `updated_at || updated_at` line is in checkRunZombies.js — line 148 in the new file. In the diff, that line appears within the added hunk, so it's commentable.

## Summary

**What the PR does** (gh-842, fixes live fa #1457): Cancelled-while-queued CI runs leave `in_progress` check-run ghosts that hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever, because branch protection takes the latest check-run per context and the tick's green-cover guards kept skipping re-dispatch. The PR adds a pure gate-ghost classifier (`js/common/checkRunZombies.js`), wires it into both skip paths in `validate_pr` (`skipIfGreenCi` and `skipIfValidatedHead` are voided when zombies hold the gate), and documents the behavior in `sm_github.json` livedoc.

**Verification performed**:
- Read the full diff via `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (the `pr_diff.txt` was truncated)
- Deep-read the classifier, the `smAgent.js` integration, and both test files
- Ran the new tests locally via the Node harness: **all 19 classifier tests + 3 smAgent replay tests pass**; the single failure (`assert.doesNotThrow` at `test_smAgent.js:6678`) is a pre-existing Node-harness gap untouched by this PR
- Checked ticket ACs: AC1/AC2/AC3 covered by L1+L2 tests; AC4 is live-soak per the ticket's own plan

**Key design strengths**: every unprovable case in `classify()` fails safe toward live (AC2), the voided skips fall through to the unchanged guarded dispatch path (AC3's anti-double-dispatch guards intact), and probe degradation keeps legacy behavior with a next-tick retry.

**One suggestion** (inline, `checkRunZombies.js:148`): duplicated `state.updated_at || state.updated_at` fallback — the second entry was clearly meant to be `updatedAt` (camelCase), matching `_startedAtMs`'s tolerance in the same file. No runtime impact today (gh API is snake_case), but it would invert the fail-safe bias if the resolver ever receives camelCase run objects.
